title: Stellar radii from Stefan–Boltzmann
question: Per star (3,300–8,000 K, parallax better than 5%): is log₁₀ radius_sb a line of slope 1 in log₁₀ radius_gspphot, and what is α in log L = α log M + c for main-sequence stars?

issues.text: The mass–luminosity slope uses FLAME masses, which come from models fitted to L and T.
issues.fix: Read α as the models' slope; a test needs dynamical masses (data).

alternatives.question: Do giants and dwarfs at the same temperature differ in luminosity by the square of their radius ratio?
Does α from eclipsing or astrometric binaries' dynamical masses match the FLAME slope?

hypotheses.statement: The Stefan–Boltzmann radius rises one-for-one with Gaia's spectral radius (log–log slope 1).
On the main sequence, log L rises with log M with slope α between 3 and 5.

concepts.label: Evolutionary stage
concepts.description: FLAME's stage: main sequence, subgiant, giant.

data.request: Masses of stars in binaries from orbital solutions
data.source: Gaia DR3 nss_two_body_orbit, or DEBCat (eclipsing binaries)

method.summary: Straight lines on log–log axes; the slope's posterior against 1 (H1) and the range 3–5 (H2).

steps.title: Sample Gaia DR3
steps.detail: random_index < 3,000,000, parallax_over_error > 20, with GSP-Phot Teff and radius.

steps.title: Derive L and R
steps.detail: lum from abs_g and bc_g; radius_sb = sqrt(lum)·(5772/teff)².

steps.title: Stages
steps.detail: evolstage_flame < 360 main sequence, < 420 subgiant, else giant.

steps.title: Fit
steps.detail: log_r_sb on log_r_gsp; log_l on log_m for the main sequence.

caveats: BC_G is fitted for 3,300–8,000 K only.
Unresolved binaries look too bright for their temperature.
